quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in mid-air by flapping their wings in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second. The Pacific Northwest is home to the beautiful Rufous Hummingbird, which migrates through the Olympic Peninsula each summer.

short_read.title: The Amazing Secret Life of Hummingbirds
short_read.teaser: These tiny jeweled birds have hearts that beat over 1,200 times per minute and memories sharp enough to remember every flower they've visited. Discover the surprising abilities of nature's smallest aviators.

medium_read.title: The Woman Who Saved Hungary's Historic Gardens
medium_read.teaser: Meet the passionate gardener who dedicated her life to preserving Hungary's centuries-old botanical treasures after World War II. Her work saved rare plants and garden designs that might otherwise have been lost forever.

long_read.title: Olympic National Park: Where Rainforest Meets the Sea
long_read.teaser: From temperate rainforests to rugged coastline, Olympic National Park contains an incredible diversity of ecosystems all within your backyard. This beautiful exploration reveals why this peninsula is unlike anywhere else on Earth.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season
port_angeles.description: August is peak pupping season for harbor seals along the Strait of Juan de Fuca! Mother seals often rest with their pups on rocky shores and beaches near Port Angeles. If you spot one, remember to watch from at least 100 yards away so the mothers feel safe caring for their babies.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute when active.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's exactly right, Barbara! Can you imagine a heart beating that fast?
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute — amazingly fast!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: It's hard to imagine, but a hummingbird's tiny heart beats about 1,200 times per minute! That's about 20 beats every second.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To power their incredible flying abilities, hummingbirds have the fastest metabolism of all animals. They must eat about half their body weight in sugar every day just to survive!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Ildiko! Pillangó is such a lovely word for such a lovely creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound like it's fluttering? (Virág means flower, madár means bird, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungary is home to over 200 species of butterflies, including the beautiful Swallowtail. Many Hungarian gardens are designed specifically to attract these colorful visitors.

puzzle_3.question: What is the only national park in the United States that contains both mountains and ocean coastline?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! You're living right next to one of America's most diverse and spectacular national parks. Olympic has it all — mountains, rainforests, and wild Pacific beaches!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's Olympic National Park, right in your own backyard! It's the only U.S. national park with both glacier-capped mountains and wild ocean coastline, making it truly special.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Olympic National Park protects nearly a million acres and contains three distinct ecosystems: subalpine forest and wildflower meadow, temperate forest, and rugged Pacific coastline. UNESCO designated it as both an International Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site.
puzzle_3.learn_more_label: Explore the park — National Park Service
